what: Every word a viewer reads in Cutling 2.0's App Store preview G, 'Every app' (card ASG166), and the seed its recordings show, in en-US, id and ja. The one source the build reads.
rule: No locale is the source the others are translated from. id and ja were written blind: each by its own writer (a separate Claude process with no tools and no file access), given only the brief below (screen, moment, meaning, budget, register, the product's own words in that language), never an English line, and never the other language's draft. en-US keeps the lines the owner saw in directions.md section G word for word.

how_to_read.overlay: Film words. Each key: devices, time in the iPhone cut, type, 'says' (what it tells a buyer), the meaning the writers wrote from, then per locale 'lines' (the line breaks to draw, measured to fit), 'text' (the same joined), and for id and ja 'back' (literal back-translation) and 'note'. Each bar is a what-line (big, ink) over a where-line (small, green).
how_to_read.seed: Content the recordings show. Each key: where it shows, 'says', then per locale the values to seed. [BLANK] and [WEEKDAY] are Cutling fill-ins (see seed.tokens).
how_to_read.written: Which writer pass produced a string. r1 is the first brief; r2 marks a key whose brief was fixed and re-run (brief_revision says why).

app_names.source: Read on 2026-11-23 from the iOS 27.2 simulator runtime (each app's <lang>.lproj/InfoPlist.strings CFBundleDisplayName) and from /System/Applications/<App>.app/Contents/Resources/InfoPlist.loctable on this Mac. iPadOS uses the iOS names.

typography.id: No dashes as connectors. Possessive -mu on a Latin product name takes a hyphen (iPhone-mu, Mac-mu).
typography.ja: 、 and 。 only; no ―. A half-width space between a Latin word and Japanese (Safari に, iPhone の, iPad と Mac も), as Cutling's 2.0 Japanese store words do; none between a digit and its counter (1回). Break only where 'lines' breaks; never let the renderer wrap Japanese on its own.

open.time: 0.0 to 2.27 s, frame 0 of the loop
open.type: iPhone 86 px bold on 760 px at x 72, y 96, lh 1.04; iPad 92 px on 1000 px
open.says: What Cutling is, in the buyer's own terms (VoC A1: 'type out the same info over and over'), and how quick it is. Leaves 'any app' to the end card, which the loop dissolves straight back into this line.
open.meaning: The things you type again and again, each a single tap away. Say only what Cutling holds and how quick it is to use. Do not say 'any app' or name an app: the end card says that, and when the film loops the end card dissolves straight back into this line, so the same point would land twice.

en-US.text: What you keep typing, one tap away
en-US.note: Owner-seen words, kept. Breaks moved so 'away' no longer sits alone on a third line and 'one tap away' stays together.

id.text: Yang sering kamu ketik, satu ketukan.
id.back: What you often / type, / one tap.
id.note: A short headline clause plus a tag, the way Indonesian ad copy runs. 'satu ketukan' is the store's own phrase. The line names what Cutling holds (what you type often) and how fast it is. It names no app and does not say 'any app', so the end card's point does not appear twice on the loop. Each line break falls at a phrase break. Units count the comma and period at 0.25 each, as narrow glyphs like a space. If your counter uses 0.52, the lines measure 5.45 and 6.49, still within 8.8.

ja.text: 何度も打つものをワンタップで
ja.back: The things (you) type again and again / with one tap
ja.note: This keeps the film's noun-stop, particle-final register, matching マップに and the end card's どれでも. It says only what Cutling holds (何度も打つもの) and how fast it is (ワンタップで). No app is named and there is no 'any app', so the end card's どれでも lands fresh when the loop returns here. The line break falls between bunsetsu. It avoids the stock 'paste in one tap' because there is no ペースト and no verb: the tap is the whole point.

open_mac.meaning: The Mac counterpart of the opening line: the things you type again and again, each one keyboard shortcut away (a Mac has no tapping). Same shape as the iPhone opening so the two read as one voice. Do not say 'any app': the Mac's own main line and end card say that.

A Mac has no tapping, so 'ketukan' is not used. It does not say 'any app'. Punctuation is counted as in open. At 0.52 per mark the last line is 7.01, within 8.1.

contacts.shows: Messages To: field (G1, G4 to contact 1; G6 to contact 5) and its suggestions; nine contacts on each store simulator.
contacts.says: Ordinary people a small seller messages; nobody real.

id.note: Ordinary names from a mix of regions. One contact has a single name with the family field empty, which is common in Indonesia. In the To: field iOS shows given then family.

ja.note: Common invented names. A Japanese-region iPhone shows them family-first with a space. Fill the よみがな fields (なかむら/ゆみ and so on) so sorting and suggestions behave as on a real phone. The five family names on the name screen are all different. Phonetic (よみがな) fields added from the names' ordinary readings.

recent_values.shows: The keyboard's name screen in G4: three keys across, two rows, the sixth is Paste. The first is tapped. Seeded as Name's recent values, most recent first.
recent_values.says: The keyboard remembers names, so the next customer is one tap.

id.note: Only first names, because the reply text already has 'Kak' before the blank, the way Indonesian sellers address customers. Each is at most 3.22 units.

ja.note: The honorific now lives in the reply text, right after the blank, instead of inside each saved name. This is how Japanese shop templates are written (〇〇様、…). It also means that for a new customer the seller types only the family name, which is natural on a Japanese keyboard, and no saved name carries a 様 the seller did not type. These are the family names of contacts 1 to 5. Each is 2 units.

blank_label.shows: The pill and the name screen's sentence in G4 (the blank's label before a name is picked).

ja.text: 名前

blank_label.note: Data, not written: the app's own default label for a new Ask Each Time blank, String(localized: "Name") in FillInSheets.swift, which is Nama and 名前 in id.lproj and ja.lproj. Insert the blank from the editor's Variables (Ask Each Time) so it carries Cutling's marker and draws as a pill.

tokens.[BLANK]: An Ask Each Time blank labelled blank_label, inserted from the editor's Variables.
tokens.[WEEKDAY]: A date variable in the Day format (EEEE) set to tomorrow (+1 day); Cutling types it in the system language: Friday, Jumat, 金曜日. The recording day decides which weekday shows.

cutlings.says: The thing everybody saves first, typed into Maps' search.
cutlings.meaning: Name: what the person calls the key for their own home address. Text: a made-up home address in this country's usual written form, short enough for one search line, with a flat or unit number. The street and area may be ordinary names that exist somewhere; no famous place and no real building name.

id.back_text: Kenanga St. Block C2 No. 5, Depok
id.note: This is a housing-estate address. 'Blok C2 No. 5' stands in for the unit number, since most Indonesians live in houses. Name 6.07, text 15.01 units.

ja.name: 自宅の住所
ja.text: 東京都練馬区豊玉北4-21-6 203
ja.note: The usual written form: prefecture, ward, town, block numbers with half-width hyphens, then the room number after a space. The ward and town are ordinary and real so Maps resolves it. The numbers are invented. About 14.6 units.

cutlings.says: A seller's everyday reply with the customer's name left for Cutling to ask.
cutlings.meaning: Name: what a small online clothing seller would call this saved reply. Text: the seller's message to a customer saying their order ships on a given day, with two pieces Cutling fills: [BLANK] where the customer's name goes, typed as one of recent_values, and [WEEKDAY] which Cutling types as tomorrow's weekday in this language's own form (Indonesian: Jumat; Japanese: 金曜日). Write the sentence around them so it reads right with a real value in place.
cutlings.brief_revision: r2 (2026-11-23): r1's unit budget undercounted Latin text; replaced with a measured point budget.

en-US.name: Order update
en-US.filled_example: Hi Maya, your order ships Friday.

id.name: Jadwal kirim
id.filled_example: Kak Rina, paketnya kami kirim Jumat ya.
id.back_text: Sis/Bro [name], the package we send [weekday] okay.
id.note: Still the online-seller voice: it opens with 'Kak' and the name, as sellers do in chat, and ends on 'ya'. 'Halo' is dropped because 'Kak Rina,' is itself a normal greeting. 'Paketnya' (the parcel) replaces 'pesanannya'. It is shorter and fits a shipping message better. The verb stays active ('kami kirim'). Filled with Rina and Jumat it is 39 characters, about 330 pt at the measured r1 rate of 8.5 pt per character. The widest case uses a 5-letter recent name (Dimas, Fitri) and a 6-letter weekday (Selasa, Minggu). That is 41 characters, about 349 pt, still under 360. On screen the pill now reads 'Kak [Nama]'.

ja.name: 発送連絡
ja.text: [BLANK]様、ご注文の品は[WEEKDAY]に発送いたします。
ja.filled_example: 中村様、ご注文の品は金曜日に発送いたします。
ja.back_text: Nakamura-sama, (your) ordered goods (topic) on Friday (we humbly) ship.
ja.note: 様 moved out of the names and into the text, right after [BLANK]. On the reply screen the pill reads 名前 followed by 様, which looks like an ordinary shop template. The text keeps business keigo (ご注文, 発送いたします), with no spaces around the filled values. The name is 4 units. The filled text is 22 units, within 23.

brief.film: Cutling 2.0 App Store preview G, 'Every app'. 22.7 s, 30 fps, autoplays muted and loops, in App Store search results (a third of the phone's width) and on the product page. The viewer is a stranger who has never had Cutling, scrolling past, reading at a glance. Cutling is a keyboard for iPhone and iPad (on the Mac a picker opened with Command-Shift-V) that holds the things a person types again and again (addresses, account numbers, replies, photos) as keys: tap a key and the whole text is typed into whatever app is open. New in 2.0: a saved reply can hold a blank, and when you tap that reply the keyboard first asks who it is for, showing names used before so one tap picks one, then types the whole reply. In the film the Cutling keyboard holds still at the bottom while Apple's own apps change above it, one app every 2.27 s. Above the screen, two lines of type: a big line (black) says what went in, a smaller line under it (green) says which app it went into. The film ends on a card: a big line, a smaller green line, the app icon and the name Cutling. iPhone, iPad and Mac each get their own cut.

register.id: The store page speaking to one person, 'kamu', everyday but standard spelling (tidak or tak, not nggak; saja, not aja), active verbs, as Cutling's 2.0 store words already read ('Balasan disimpan sekali, namanya beda tiap pakai.', 'Cutling tanya nama, isi tanggal hari ini sendiri, lalu ketik sisanya.'). Seed texts are what a real person would have saved for themselves, in their own voice.
register.ja: Store captions: short, plain, no cheerleading. Choose noun-stop captions or です・ます sentences and hold one register across every line of the film. Seed texts are what a real person would have saved for themselves, in their own voice; a shop's messages to a customer use the polite business register.

rules: No source string exists. Write what a person in this language would put on this screen at this moment. Do not ask for an English version.
Every line must read at a glance at search-result size: the fewest words that carry the meaning.
No price, no date with a year, no 'free', no 'subscription', no real business, no real person, no real bank's name, no famous place.

Do not say any of these ideas in their stock phrasing, which rival apps already use: 'write a reply once', 'leave blanks', 'fill in the blanks', 'save it once', 'copy it anytime', 'paste in one tap', 'type less'.

Indonesian: no dashes as connectors; a comma, a conjunction or a new sentence. Avoid stiff passives (dilakukan, dapat dilakukan) and needless English loans where Indonesians use the native word; keep loans Indonesians really use.
Japanese: 、 and 。 only, no ― as a connector; no needless katakana loanwords; never mix です・ます with だ・である.

Overlay lines are given as an array of display lines. Japanese: break only between bunsetsu, never inside a word, never start a line with 、。ー or a small kana. Indonesian: break between words where the phrase breaks.
Each overlay line's budget is in full-width units: one CJK character or kana = 1.0; a Latin capital or digit = 0.62; a Latin lowercase letter = 0.52; a space = 0.25; a full-width 、 or 。 = 1.0.

findings: Japanese G4 shows a stray space. The keyboard's smart spacing (CutlingKeyboard/KeyboardViewController.swift, static func spaced, lines 640-652) adds ' ' before any cutling whose first character is not punctuation when the text before ends in a non-space. After the Japanese order reply ends in 「。」, tapping the thanks types '…発送いたします。 お買い上げ…', which reads as a typo to a Japanese viewer (and hits every ja and zh user who types two cutlings in a row). Either the app skips the space after CJK text and punctuation, or the ja take ends the order reply with a line break so the thanks starts on its own line (Japanese shop messages often do that); this file seeds the reply without one.

The fill-in header fits whole in every language. It has 370 pt on the 440 pt store iPhone (440 - 2x6 padding - 44 close - 6 spacing - 2x4 padding, FillInPanel.swift and KeyStyle) and drops whole space-separated words when it is too wide. Widest case at 16 pt SF Pro, measured in Chrome: en 317 ('Wednesday'), id 344 ('Kak Dimas, ... Selasa ya.'), ja 350. The first Indonesian reply measured 391 and would have lost its day, so it was rewritten shorter.

Addresses may resolve to a real lot in Maps and in Calendar's Location suggestions in every language (14 Linden Road, Jl. Kenanga Blok C2 No. 5 Depok, 東京都練馬区豊玉北4-21-6). The numbers are invented and no building is named; directions.md's recording rule applies: if Maps pins a home, cut before the result list.

Indonesian register is split. The app's id strings say 'Anda' (89 of 93 person references in Cutling/id.lproj), the store words say 'kamu' (2.0 event words, these overlays), so G4 shows the keyboard's 'Ketik di Keyboard Biasa Anda' under a '-mu' line for about a second. This predates the change and is left as it is here.

The stand-in's iPad where-line 'in Calendar, on iPad' is dropped: iPad previews play on the iPad's page, so the iPad uses the same where-lines as the iPhone. directions.md lists one iPad take (G7, 3 s used), so the iPad film needs more takes to reach 15 s; every bar's words carry 'ipad' in devices for that.
The English refund holder changes from the stand-in's 'Sam Okafor' to 'Nora Okafor', because Sam is also a customer on the name screen and the account is the keyboard owner's.

checks.blind: The writer prompts (scratch prompt-*.txt) were grepped for the English lines and seed names (Maya, Linden, Pottery class, Order update, one tap away, Any app): 0 hits. id and ja ran as separate processes with no tools.
checks.back_translation: Every id and ja back-translation was compared with its key's meaning. Four briefs were wrong and were fixed and re-run, never edited toward the English: (1) open and open_mac: r1's meaning added 'in any app', which repeats the end card across the loop seam; (2) id size chart heads: r1's 5-unit budget forced 'Dada' for 'Lebar Dada'; (3) ja honorific: r1 gave no facts on where 様 goes, so r2 gave them and the writer moved it into the reply; (4) id order reply: r1's unit budget undercounted Latin text, so r2 used a measured 360 pt budget.
checks.tells: human-prose Final check and language-surface-forms were run on both: no dashes in id, only 、。 in ja, one register per language (id kamu with standard spelling; ja noun-stop captions, business keigo in the seller's seed), no 'not X but Y' frames, no filler, and no rival phrasing.
checks.fit: Every overlay line in all three locales was set at the film's type (stage.js S.text: -apple-system, letter-spacing -0.02em, sizes from g-every-app.js) in headless Chrome and measured against its measure: 0 lines over (121 device-locale lines). The sheets were looked at for each locale.
checks.not_checked: Seed text on the real keyboard cards and the size chart image are not rendered here: that happens in the takes. Card names are at most 7 CJK characters or 15 Latin characters.
